name: Synthwave Grid
tagline: 80s outrun: a striped neon sun, an endless scrolling grid, chrome type and VHS glitch cuts.
description: Retro-futurist style for synth plugins, retro games, music drops and night events. A magenta-to-gold striped sun sinks behind wireframe mountains while a neon perspective grid scrolls toward camera; chrome italic display type and a glowing script subtitle punch in on VHS tracking glitches, under scanlines and a fake camcorder HUD.

display.usage: Chrome titles 170–230px, skewX(-10deg), gradient clipped to text with a white 2px stroke

body.usage: Neon script subtitles 120–190px, rotated -7°, overlapping the chrome title's lower right

accent.usage: Cyan neon-tube feature words 150–170px, one per beat

mono.usage: Camcorder HUD 46–54px and tracked caption bands, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.32em

transitions: VHS glitch cut: 0.13s of hard x/skew jitter on the whole world, screen-blended colour bars and a tracking-noise band sweeping down
hard cut between feature words, each with its own mini glitch
textAnimations: chrome squash-slam: scaleX 1.7 / scaleY 0.6 → 1 with expo.out in 0.6s
specular shine sweeps across the chrome gradient (background-position) over ~1s
script subtitle writes on with a left-to-right clip-path inset wipe
neon words punch in from scale 1.35 and their glow flickers up

rhythm.notes: Atmospheric opener (~1.7s) while the sun rises, a 2.7s hero title hold, then rapid 0.55s feature beats, and a chrome end card. Grid, sun stripes and timecode never stop moving.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Set: sky gradient #07021a → #5a0f6e → #ff5f9e with the horizon at y≈640 and a seeded starfield, a sun r≈290 with a #fff07a → #ff9d3c → #ff2a8a gradient and black mask bands (3→27px tall) scrolling upward, and wireframe mountains in #12042b with #ff3fd8 ridges and #2ff3ff struts. The subject sits in front of this world.
- The floor is one wide div with transform: perspective(520px) rotateX(78deg), transform-origin 50% 0, magenta vertical and cyan horizontal 4px gradient lines; tween only its background-position (linear, never stops). Add a pink haze at the horizon.
- Chrome type: Bungee 170–230px, skewX(-10deg) on an inner span, text-clipped gradient #f8fcff → #9cd9ff → #24165c (hard horizon at 51%) → #ff7fd4 → white, white 2px stroke, a #3b0b62 7px drop shadow plus magenta bloom. It squash-slams from scaleX 1.7 / scaleY 0.6 with expo.out in 0.6s, then a white specular band sweeps across it over ~1s.
- Script subtitle in Mr Dafoe 120–190px, pale pink #ffe1f6 with layered #ff4fd8 / #ff2fa0 glows, rotated -7° and overlapping the chrome title's lower right, revealed with a left-to-right clip-path wipe. Short feature words in Monoton cyan neon (150–170px), one per 0.5–0.6s beat, punching in from scale 1.35 as the glow flickers up.
- Every cut is a VHS glitch (≤0.16s): world x ±34px + skewX ±9°, colour bars in screen blend, a tracking-noise band sweeping down.
- Pacing: an atmospheric ~1.7s opener, a long hero title hold, rapid 0.5–0.6s beats, then a chrome end card. Grid, sun stripes and timecode never stop moving.
- Optional motif: a camcorder HUD outside the glitching layer (VT323 46–54px uppercase: ▶ PLAY, a running SP timecode, a date and a channel number that changes per cut).
- Always overlay 2px scanlines (28% black) and a vignette. Avoid flat backgrounds, sans-serif body copy and pastel colours.
example: The preview is a launch for a retro synth plugin: the striped sun rises over the grid, the chrome product name slams in with a neon script subtitle, feature words flash on glitch cuts, and it ends on a chrome end card. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
